recent_tasks.instruction_summary: You need to create a visual diagram summarizing the pricing structure from the MCC 150072 price list in `~/Desktop/test_files/libreoffice_docx/price.docx`. Open the file in LibreOf
Open `~/Desktop/test_files/drawio/test.drawio` in draw.io. Using Extras > Edit Diagram (or the XML editor), inspect the raw XML of the diagram. Count the total number of `<mxCell>`
Open `~/Desktop/test_files/drawio/test.drawio` in draw.io. Add a new page named "Summary" to the diagram (in addition to any existing pages). On the Summary page, create a flowchar
Open `~/Desktop/test_files/pptx/186_3_Gold.pptx` in LibreOffice Impress and note the exact title text of slide 1 and the current background color name shown in the Properties panel

drawio XML parsing: Draw.io .drawio files may store mxGraphModel either as direct XML elements or as compressed/base64 URL-encoded text inside <diagram>; evaluators should handle both forms before searching for mxCell nodes.
connector direction: When the task requires arrows from one box to others, verify edge mxCell source and target ids in the required direction and inspect arrow style, rather than accepting either orientation as a connection.
connector direction verification: For draw.io diagrams, checking only mxCell source/target links is not enough for arrow tasks; verify the edge style's endArrow/startArrow semantics align with the required direction, and do not unconditionally accept reversed source/target edges.
diagram shape and connector verification: For draw.io tasks requiring boxes and arrows, checking mxCell vertex geometry and source/target edges is useful, but a stronger evaluator should also inspect style attributes for rectangle-like shapes and arrowhead properties such as endArrow not being none.
draw.io XML count task: For count-audit tasks, do not add a separate source-file parseability rule that awards credit independent of the required output artifact; it can make the initial state pass partially. Compute the ground truth inside the artifact-validation rule instead.
drawio XML mxCell count verification: For draw.io files, robust evaluators should parse both uncompressed XML mxCell elements and compressed <diagram> payloads; output text checks should validate the raw file content, not just non-empty lines, when the instruction requires exactly one line.
compressed diagram XML verification: For draw.io .drawio files, robust evaluators should parse both inline mxCell XML and each <diagram> payload, including base64 raw-deflate content, then count mxCell elements from the decoded XML.
exact one-line text output: When verifying exactly one optional trailing newline, avoid raw.rstrip('\n') because it permits multiple trailing newlines; instead explicitly allow raw == expected or raw == expected + '\n'.
diagram XML parsing: draw.io <diagram> contents may be compressed/encoded text rather than nested mxCell XML; evaluators should decode base64/raw-deflate/URL-encoded mxGraphModel content before checking cells.
connector label verification: Connector labels in draw.io may be stored either as the edge mxCell value or as a child vertex mxCell whose parent is the edge, so evaluators should handle both representations and exclude such label cells from shape counts.
compressed diagram parsing: draw.io mxfile diagram text is commonly base64 of raw-deflated URL-encoded XML; after zlib decompression evaluators should apply urllib.parse.unquote before XML parsing.
page addition verification: For tasks that require adding a new draw.io page in addition to existing pages, the evaluator should anchor against original diagram names/counts or otherwise verify existing pages were preserved, not just that the new page name exists.
edge labels and shape counting: When verifying exactly N shapes in draw.io, exclude connector label child mxCells whose parent is an edge or whose geometry is relative=1; otherwise a valid labeled connector can be counted as an extra vertex shape.
drawio XML verification: A .drawio file may contain mxCell elements directly or may store a compressed/URL-encoded mxGraphModel inside a <diagram> element; evaluators should decode both forms before searching for shapes and connectors.
compressed .drawio parsing: For standard compressed draw.io files, decode diagram text by base64-decoding, raw zlib inflating with windowBits -15, then URL-decoding the decompressed string before parsing the inner mxGraphModel XML.
exact shape count and edge validation: For draw.io tasks requiring a specific number of shapes, parse mxCell vertices and enforce the exact count and expected styles/labels; avoid fallback edge checks that can credit unrelated connectors.
